text:
First of all thank you for testing it at Cyberpunk 2077 1080p RT Overdrive.
I assume the rest of the settings are at max too.
I do have a question.  The 12:39 numbers where you speak about it, show that natively the latency is higher than even with 4x frame generation.  As I have no experience with the technology, would that mean the "experience" would be better with frame generation?  The latency even at 4X frame gen is 12ms less. 
I like this card.  I admit a large part of why I like it is the power consumption, not requiring that stu of a special connector, and of course the longevity of Nvidia's driver support.

Thanks for another great review.  Not all mention or understand the extra cost in the product and the power consumption here in Euroland.
author: @TrusteftTech

text: The experience with DLSS with 4x FG you see at 12:39 is definitely better than native, and you can argue that it can look a bit better than just using DLSS (53 fps, 39 ms), but it's just not nearly the same as playing at lower settings (like high settings, no RT, ~140fps, lower latency). I'd say it's worth trying out and seeing what works for you, how you experience latency and MFG seems to be pretty subjective.

text:
Not your fault, but honestly the 5060 Ti 16GB is pretty boring. (As is the 5000 series in generel)
If the 16GB version was 50-100€ cheaper than the 4060 Ti 16 GB version the ok. ~10% but at least it is a lot cheaper. (But if I look at the market right now, the price is about the same)

Also if you already have a 1070, 1080, 2070 super, 3060 or similar (there are many card in that range) then the 5060 Ti is just double the speed and double the VRAM or maybe a little less depending on the card. And we are talking cards that a 6-8 years old at this point. Cards that cost about the same as a cheap 5060 Ti 16 GB.
That is just not that exciting. I feel like a lot of people would be better of spending a bit more and get a 9070 XT or 5070 ti. They are very expensive, but they are also much faster. And the price per frame is about the same, so you are not really paying more for the extra performance, as you would do for the 5080 and 5090. And if GPU's will have the same improvement over the next 8 years as they have had the last 8 years, then you might end up being happy with that card much longer. But it requires a larger investment up front, and not everyone can do that.

On the other hand if you don't already have a GPU, then the 4060 Ti 16 GB actually looks ok. You can play a lot of games at good settings and it is much much better than not having a GPU at all.
But I don't think anyone will look back and think of the 5000 series as one of the all time greats.

text:
@TechTesters  I am not that hopeful about the AMD 9060 XT. It does look a little too much like a 7600 XT to me.
Also Nvidia tend to only make corrections with new cards. And a 5060 Ti Super is probably 1-1.5 year away even if AMD's 9060 XT is a beast.

But I am hoping that AMD will sell a lot of 9070 XT's and get that card in the top 15 on the steam hardware survey. But it will take a long time before gamers will consider AMD and Nvidia as equals. Many young gamers haver never tried playing games on a AMD card at all.

And even if we get competition between AMD and Nvidia all the GPU's are still produced by TSMC anyway.

I think you are right for new buyers. But maybe some people that already have a GPU have or will hold out maybe a year more to save up a little extra such that they might be able to get a 620$ card.

There is also a world where trade wars or Invasion of Taiwan will slow down improvements in chip production making people very happy that they got a 5000/9000 series card before availability got completely impossible and the generational gains evaporated completely. And in that situation any 16 GB card would have been a good buy. 😱
